svg.text: Figure 1a — Runtime Architecture and Threat Overview
Juice Shop · 20.1.1 · 7 components · 16 data flows · 4 trust boundaries · 63 threats in the model

g.title: Trust boundary crossing: tb-1 External → C-04; tb-3 External → C-02; tb-4 External → C-03; tb-5 External → C-02

df-002: Authenticated REST API calls (products, basket, orders, profile, feedback) (HTTPS) df-013: Unauthenticated REST API access — registration, public product listing, feedback submission (HTTPS) df-002 authentication: JWT RS256 token from localStorage injected as Authorization: Bearer header; evidence: frontend/src/app/Services/request.interceptor.ts:16, lib/insecurity.ts:156 df-002 access group: API calls (authenticated or anonymous); alternatives; step n/a df-013 authentication: endpoints such as POST /api/Users (registration) and POST /api/Feedbacks require no authentication per route inventory signals; evidence: server.ts:408 df-013 access group: API calls (authenticated or anonymous); alternatives; step n/a

df-003: Password-based login — POST /rest/user/login with email and password credentials (HTTPS) df-004: TOTP second-factor verification — POST /rest/2fa/verify with tmpToken and totpToken (HTTPS) df-003 authentication: email + MD5-hashed password submitted to login endpoint; SQL injection vulnerability present (raw query at routes/login.ts:34); evidence: routes/login.ts:34 df-003 access group: Credentials (2FA if enrolled); sequence; step 1 df-004 authentication: Interim tmpToken (JWT type=password_valid_needs_second_factor_token) plus TOTP code validated with otplib verifySync; evidence: routes/2fa.ts:20 df-004 access group: Credentials (2FA if enrolled); sequence; step 2

df-005: OAuth-derived login — POST /rest/user/login using password derived from base64-reversed email (HTTPS) df-005 authentication: no real credential: password is reversed base64 of email, trivially predictable (CWE-522); evidence: frontend/src/app/oauth/oauth.component.ts:30

df-006: Socket.IO WebSocket connection for challenge-solved notifications and client-side challenge verification events (WebSocket) df-006 authentication: no authentication check on WebSocket connection or events; evidence: lib/startup/registerWebsocketEvents.ts:23

df-007: Sequelize ORM queries for products, orders, basket items, feedback, users, and challenge state (SQLite) df-007 authentication: in-process SQLite file access; no network authentication; evidence: models/index.ts:33

df-008: Raw SQL user lookup during login — SELECT with unsanitized email and password (injectable query) (SQLite) df-008 authentication: in-process SQLite file access; no network authentication; evidence: models/index.ts:33
df-009: MarsDB queries for product reviews collection and orders collection (MarsDB) df-009 authentication: in-process MarsDB access; no network authentication; evidence: data/mongodb.ts:9

df-010: Streaming chat completion request to OpenAI-compatible LLM endpoint for /rest/chat handler (HTTPS) df-010 authentication: API key or no auth depending on provider; LLM base URL from config, no key confirmed in source; evidence: routes/chat.ts:109

df-014: OAuth authorization (HTTPS) df-014 authentication: The identity provider authenticates the user at its sign-in endpoint; evidence: frontend/src/app/login/login.component.ts:31, frontend/src/app/login/login.component.ts:148
df-015: OAuth profile request (HTTPS) df-015 authentication: The provider checks the OAuth access token sent with the request; evidence: frontend/src/app/Services/user.service.ts:68
Internet Attacker → C-02 · Express API Server: scenario 1, 2, 3, 4, 5; its findings also affect C-03 · Authentication and Session Handler
Internet Attacker → C-07 · Web3 / NFT / Wallet Surface: scenario 2, 4
Internet Attacker → C-03 · Authentication and Session Handler: scenario 2, 4, 6
Internet Attacker → C-04 · Socket.IO Real-time Channel: scenario 4
Internet Attacker → Juice Shop User: scenario 6, 7
C-01 · Angular SPA Frontend: JWT Authentication Tokens
Further capabilities: XML parsing — evidence: routes/fileUpload.ts:76; Server-side templates — evidence: routes/userProfile.ts:87 (reported finding)
C-02 · Express API Server: Application Configuration and Secrets
C-02 · Express API Server: User-Uploaded Files
C-03 · Authentication and Session Handler: JWT Signing Key Pair
C-05 · SQLite / Sequelize Data Store: User Credentials
C-05 · SQLite / Sequelize Data Store: Payment Card Data
C-05 · SQLite / Sequelize Data Store: Personal Profile Data
C-05 · SQLite / Sequelize Data Store: Challenge Progress and Score Data
C-05 · SQLite / Sequelize Data Store: Product Catalog and Reviews
C-06 · MarsDB Embedded Document Store: Product Catalog and Reviews
Anonymous or registered user interacting with the Juice Shop SPA through a web browser. Includes CTF participants, security trainees, and automated scanner clients.

Google accounts OAuth 2.0 authorization server used by the Angular frontend for browser-only login. No server-side OAuth code path exists; the frontend derives a password from the returned email and calls the standard login endpoint.
OpenAI-compatible LLM inference endpoint (or local Ollama) used by the /rest/chat route for AI-SDK streaming chat completions. Base URL is read from application config.
OAuth authorization: https://accounts.google.com. Activation depends on deployment configuration.
OAuth profile request: https://www.googleapis.com. Activation depends on deployment configuration.
Application role with elevated rights, evidenced by its access check.

Google OAuth df-011: Browser redirect to Google OAuth authorization endpoint to initiate login (HTTPS); Google accounts OAuth2 authorization request; browser-only, no server-side code exchange df-012: OAuth callback delivers Google profile data (email) to Angular oauth component (HTTPS); Google-issued authorization code / profile; frontend derives weak password from returned email

C-01 · Angular SPA Frontend df-011: Browser redirect to Google OAuth authorization endpoint to initiate login (HTTPS); Google accounts OAuth2 authorization request; browser-only, no server-side code exchange df-012: OAuth callback delivers Google profile data (email) to Angular oauth component (HTTPS); Google-issued authorization code / profile; frontend derives weak password from returned email

g.text: data flow · classification colour · two heads = bidirectional
trust boundary crossed between these columns
dashed outline = zone, not itself a boundary
solid = direct attack · dashed = via user
STRIDE-per-element: filled = threats found in that class
All Critical · High fills to 5 · +N = omitted High categories
counts on a node = threats per severity · ①–⑨ = attack scenario
badges also count scenarios that hit an asset stored there
Dynamic code evaluation = runs runtime data as program code
LLM + tools = model calls with executable application tools
Most security-critical functions always shown (at most 5), others up
to 3 labels per element: most critical first, then most severe linked
finding; +N = further labels, listed under Further capabilities.
Functions may go undetected: a missing label does not mean absence.
Matching E-labels indicate a connection; lines omitted.
